Q1: Creosote presents known hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity (CMR), and inhalation (IHL). It also shows expanded hazards (Tier 2) for environmental effects (ENV) and dermal/eye exposure (SKN). Data is deficient (Tier 4) for endocrine disruption (EDC) and organ/systemic hazards (OGN), while oral hazards (ORL) are considered low to moderate (Tier 3).
Q2: Creosote is listed by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) as "probably carcinogenic to humans" (Group 2A). It does not appear on any lists specifically designating it as a low hazard chemical.
Q3: While Creosote has undergone rigorous evaluation by the EPA's IRIS program and has 22 toxicity records, its characterization is otherwise limited. It has zero literature references, an "unspecified" molecular formula, and is classified as a poorly defined "Manual Registration" and "Registered Concept," with remaining data gaps for some hazard classes.
